bindings.label: Patient has recurrent ankle swelling, painful nodules on legs and feet, progression to painful leg ulcers, and oral and vaginal ulcerations
A 30-year-old woman has a 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and intermittent painful and tender nodules on legs and feet; symptoms worsened during two pregnancies carried to term.

One and a half years before admission, nodules progressed to painful leg ulcers and she developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations; previous treatments included wound care, leg compression, systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin, and rivaroxaban.

Physical examination showed large, extremely tender, irregularly shaped circumferential leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and fibrinous base; reticulated erythema and purpura on hands; faintly erythematous blanching macules and papules coalescing into patches and thin plaques on bilateral thighs; genital and oral ulcers present.
Skin biopsy shows atypical T-cell infiltrate with aberrant CD4/CD8 coexpression and abnormal flow cytometry
Patient has T-cell lymphoma with secondary vasculitic ulceration
Doppler ultrasound shows venous stasis is secondary rather than a primary thrombotic process
TCR gene rearrangement and bone marrow studies are unavailable, so T-cell clonality is not definitively confirmed
Skin biopsy histology shows a monomorphic perivascular and adnexal atypical T-cell infiltrate with aberrant CD4/CD8 coexpression
Pathologist analysis concludes Behçet disease and primary vasculitis/thrombotic APS lack supporting evidence and are basically excluded
